title: Fact, opinion and claims
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:49Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The closest bank point, Writing about a text, teaches how to structure a literary analysis paragraph (claim, evidence, explanation) and does not teach distinguishing facts from opinions or checking claims presented as fact, so the new point needs its own card.

draft.title: Fact, opinion and claims
card: a statement that can be checked and shown to be true or false, such as the date of an event or a measured amount.
a person's view or judgement, such as that a film is boring. It cannot be proved true or false, and words such as best, worst or should often signal it.
a statement that is put forward as true. A claim can be written as if it were a fact, but it still needs evidence before readers should accept it.
To test a claim, ask who says it, what evidence supports it, and whether the source is reliable. A confident tone is not evidence.
draft.remember: Facts can be checked, opinions are views, and claims need evidence even when they sound certain.

opts: The new park is the best place in town to relax
The new park opened to the public in March
The new park has two playgrounds and a pond
The new park covers about five hectares
a.why: Best is a judgement that depends on the speaker's view, so it cannot be proved true or false. The other three can be checked by looking at records or by measuring.
a.clue: Which one depends on what a person likes?

b.q: A website says: 'Everyone knows that students who wear school hats get better marks.' What should a careful reader do first?
opts: Look for evidence that supports the claim
Accept it, because it is stated so confidently
Reject it, because it is an opinion
Accept it, because the word everyone shows many agree
b.why: The sentence is a claim presented as fact, so it needs evidence before it is accepted. Confident wording and everyone knows are not evidence. It is not simply an opinion, because it could be tested, but the site has not shown how.
b.clue: A confident tone does not prove anything.

a.best: The new park is the best place in town to relax

b.best: Look for evidence that supports the claim
